The door-frame knob cue borrows from the universal threshold tradition and the modern open-closed aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as next-chapter rather than literal door.

In real-world usage 🚪 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate exit-coded energy. A friend sends it on a 'next-chapter vibe 🚪' reveal. An opportunity-coded chat partner sends it on a 'threshold-coded 🚪' coded message. A coworker sends it on a 'door-moment flex 🚪' exit-coded flex. The door-frame knob cue is what makes the emoji feel exit-coded — it is not just 'door,' it is 'exit-coded next-chapter flex.'

What separates 🚪 from the rest of the household-emoji family is the threshold register. The emoji is not saying 'house' (🏠), 'bed' (🛏), or 'couch' (🛋).
